notes: This is a recall/precision checklist for evaluating extraction
quality, not an exact-match target. A correct extraction will
phrase each requirement differently from source.quote below;
source.quote only marks where in tender.txt the requirement
originates, for offset-based matching and for a human reviewer
to locate it quickly.
This list aims to be EXHAUSTIVE over bidder-facing, pre-award,
text-verifiable requirements in tender.txt -- not a representative
sample. 'Exhaustive' means every distinct checkable condition, not
every sentence: connective/scaffolding sentences that merely
introduce an already-listed item are not separately enumerated.
'excluded_clauses' below is the deliberate complement: concrete
spans a plausible bad extraction could mistake for a requirement,
even though they are government-facing instructions or post-award
clauses. Together, requirements + excluded_clauses let evaluation
classify any actual (extracted) requirement that matches neither
list as a genuine fixture gap needing manual triage, rather than
silently counting it against precision.
Several requirements (SAM registration, UEI, price schedule,
'or equal' documentation, capabilities statement) are restated
verbatim or near-verbatim two or three times across tender.txt
(Description section, Instructions to Offerors, Registration
Requirements). Each topic below anchors to ONE canonical
occurrence; a correct pipeline is expected to deduplicate the
restatements into a single Requirement, so matching an actual
requirement's citation set against this one anchor span is
sufficient -- the restatements are not separate topics.
prior_experience_count and prior_experience_poc_required were
deliberately split from what used to be a single
'prior_experience_minimum_3_with_poc' topic: the source sentence
bundles two independently-checkable conditions (how many/how
recent/how similar the references are, vs. whether each reference
includes contact information), and the real application evidence
satisfies one but not the other for the third reference. A single
blended topic could not express that split outcome; see
expected_verdicts.json.
prior_experience_count.is_mandatory is a deliberate ambiguity, not
an error: the CHECKLIST FOR QUOTE SUBMITTAL section states
'Three prior experiences' unqualified (source.quote below), but
the later 'TO SUBMIT AN OFFER' section (item 3) softens this to
'preferably a minimum of 3'. The tender itself is internally
inconsistent here. is_mandatory is set true, anchored to the
checklist wording, but a pipeline that reasonably classifies this
as non-mandatory given the later softening should not be scored
as simply wrong.
submission_deadline_and_channel is a deliberate test of false-
compliance avoidance: application.txt (a capabilities-statement-
style document) has no reason to contain submission-timestamp or
channel metadata, so the expected verdict is
insufficient_information -- a pipeline that guesses 'compliant'
with zero supporting evidence has failed this case, even though
the requirement itself is real and mandatory.
site_visit_expectation lives in excluded_clauses, not in
requirements: the site visit happens before/outside the
application and the tender never asks the bidder to say anything
about it in their quote, so it imposes no obligation on the
application's content at all. It stays a deliberate negative
case -- 'the site visit is urged and expected' reads like bidder-
facing obligation language, exactly what a weak extraction could
mistake for a requirement -- but the correct fixture home for
that trap is excluded_clauses, not a requirements entry with
is_mandatory: false.
contractor_core_data and final_offer_total_no_alternates were
added after auditing a real run's 'unexplained' actual
requirements against tender.txt directly: both are genuine
bidder-facing content the earlier 13/14-topic list simply missed,
not restatements of an existing topic anchored elsewhere.
contractor_core_data covers the '(c) Contractor Core Data' fill-in
block (company name, Cage Code/UEI, POC, POC email/phone) as one
topic rather than four, since they are one contiguous form with
no independent pass/fail meaning per field.
final_offer_total_no_alternates is related to but distinct from
price_schedule_complete: it is specifically about submitting one
final total with no alternate quotes, not about filling out the
price schedule form itself.
